introHeading: The mirror booth, built for the drive out to Long Island
introParas: The magic mirror is a natural fit for the range of events Long Island brings us — a black-tie wedding on a Gold Coast estate lawn, a Sweet Sixteen at a Nassau catering hall, a brand activation tucked into a Hamptons summer share. The gold frame and full-length format read well in a formal ballroom and a tented lawn alike, and the touchscreen's animated prompts and voice guidance keep the line moving whether the crowd is fifty guests or three hundred.

Because the drive out is real — the LIE, the Northern State, whatever route your venue sits off of — we treat a Long Island booking differently from a five-mile Brooklyn run. We build in a wider arrival window than we would in the city, so a backed-up lane or a Friday-afternoon crawl toward the Hamptons never turns into a late setup. Estate and mansion venues that want the mirror set up outdoors need level ground, shade for the touchscreen and a dedicated power run, which we confirm with you well before the date rather than discovering it on arrival.

Setup still takes about 20 minutes once we're in the room, and we still arrive a full hour ahead of your start time — that buffer sits on top of the extra driving time, not instead of it. The booth wants a 10ft x 10ft footprint, or 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance where a hall floor runs tighter, plus a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet. Travel across Nassau, Suffolk and the Hamptons is quoted from your venue's ZIP code before you book, so the number you see up front is the number on the invoice.

faqHeading: Mirror Photo Booth on Long Island — FAQ

faqs.q: Do you actually travel all the way out to Long Island, or just the western end?
faqs.a: We serve all of Long Island — Nassau, Suffolk and the Hamptons — as a standard part of our service area, not a special-request trip. It's a longer drive than a Brooklyn booking, so we build extra time into our schedule for it, but the booking process and pricing structure are the same.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee to Long Island?
faqs.a: There's no flat borough-style rate the way there is closer to Brooklyn — travel across Nassau, Suffolk and the Hamptons is quoted from your venue's exact ZIP code before you book, so you see the real number up front rather than a surprise line item on the invoice.

faqs.q: Can the mirror booth be set up outdoors at a Gold Coast estate or Hamptons venue?
faqs.a: Yes, with a few conditions — level ground, shade for the touchscreen, and a dedicated power run rather than sharing a circuit with a tent's lighting or a DJ setup. We'll walk through your outdoor space with you before booking to confirm it's a good fit.

faqs.q: What if our venue is far enough out that setup timing is tight?
faqs.a: We build a wider arrival buffer into Long Island bookings than we would for a closer venue, specifically so traffic on the LIE or a Friday crawl toward the Hamptons doesn't turn into a late setup. We still arrive a full hour before your scheduled start time on top of that.

faqs.q: How much space does the mirror booth need at a Nassau catering hall?
faqs.a: The optimal footprint is 10ft x 10ft, which leaves room for the backdrop, props table and a red carpet if you want one. We can compress to a minimum of 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter hall floor, and we need one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with a Long Island mirror booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your rental — setup, keeping the prop table organized, helping guests use the touchscreen, and packing down at the end of the night.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for a Long Island venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we will send it over.

faqs.q: Which parts of Long Island do you cover?
faqs.a: We're regularly out across Nassau County, Suffolk County, Garden City, Huntington, the Hamptons and Great Neck. If your venue isn't on that list, ask anyway — we'll tell you honestly whether we can get there and what travel would run.

faqs.q: How long does setup take once you arrive?
faqs.a: About 20 minutes once we're in the room. If your Long Island venue needs us on site earlier than our standard hour-ahead arrival, idle time runs $150 per hour.
